scenes.heading: Understanding different trading styles and time horizons

sents.d: Understanding different trading styles and time horizons
Matching a style to your actual schedule matters more than picking the 'best' one.

Day trading, swing trading, and longer-term position trading differ mainly in time horizon — day trading closes positions within a single day, swing trading holds for days to weeks, and position trading holds for months or longer.

Each style demands a different time commitment and temperament: day trading generally requires being available and focused during market hours, while longer-term approaches require less daily attention but more patience through short-term price swings.

Choosing a style that fits your actual available time and temperament, rather than whichever style looks most exciting online, is one of the more overlooked decisions new traders make — and mismatches here are a common source of unnecessary stress and mistakes.

take: Choose a trading style that fits your schedule and temperament.
